exposure: specific clinical circumstances for cord management
presence of policies or guidelines regarding cord management
outcome: applicability of DCC in various gestational ages and clinical scenarios
cohort: The study surveyed 1050 members of the American College of Nurse-Midwives (ACNM) who responded to a national online questionnaire about their umbilical cord management practices.
finding: The practice of delayed cord clamping (DCC) significantly increased by 46% among ACNM members compared to 2000, with 98% now facilitating it for full-term vaginal births, while cord milking is less widely adopted (37% practice).
mod_finding: Midwives found it challenging to practice DCC in situations involving breech births or when the newborn needed resuscitation.
